title: French food and street names in New Orleans
summary: Light talk about red beans and rice, French street names and how stew turtle is prepared.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, that would be about our only true American music. Yeah, that's it. They brought it there. Now, those red beans and rice we were talking about, you had plenty of that. How do you like the French cooking over here? Well, that's the same.

French in New Orleans. You know, we got streets named Iberville, Bienville, and all the French people. And good cow and... You ate that? No, no, no. What is it? Stew turtle. Oh, no. Yeah. That's enough. No stew turtle. Oh, no. But they don't eat. They don't just throw him in there and cook him, you know. No? No. What do they do to him? Well, they take the little house off his back.
